resources.string: Archive INA — “Comment compter comme les Shadoks ?”
Four words, and not one more
Arithmetic had always given the Shadoks a good deal of trouble: they had only four words, and could not count any further than four. Professor Shadoko reformed all that.
When there is no Shadok, you say GA. When there is one Shadok more, you say BU. When there is yet one more, you say ZO. And when there is another one still, you say MEU.

And what if you add one more Shadok? There is no word left to count it. So you throw the first four into a bin and say BU BIN. To avoid confusion with the BU you started with, you add that there is no Shadok beside the bin: BU GA. That is our 4.

It carries on the same way: one bin and one Shadok beside it, BU BU, 5. One bin and two Shadoks, BU ZO, 6. Two bins and no Shadok, ZO GA, 8. Up to three bins and three Shadoks — MEU MEU, 15 — where there is no room left.
The big bin, then the super bin

By then there are too many bins to be counted. You get rid of them by throwing them into a big bin, and you write BU GA GA: one big bin, no small bin, and no Shadok beside it. That is 16. When the big bins overflow in turn, they go into a super bin: BU GA GA GA, 64.
Each bin holds four of the size below, and that is all “counting in base 4” means. A place is therefore worth four times the previous one: BuZo reads 1 × 4 + 2 = 6, and MeuMeu 3 × 4 + 3 = 15.

The lesson stops at whole numbers; a calculator does not. To the right of the point, the places are worth a quarter, a sixteenth, and so on: Ga.Zo is 2 ÷ 4, that is one half. Since 4 = 2², a fraction is written exactly only when its denominator is a power of two. A third never terminates: the calculator marks it with ≈ rather than passing a rounding off as an exact value.
Hours and minutes are each converted as a whole number, not digit by digit: 14:35 gives MeuZo:ZoGaMeu, because 14 is written 32 and 35 is written 203.

The reform was not to everyone\'s taste. The plumber held that the children were being taught nothing but nonsense, and wanted Professor Shadoko burned. It was decided unanimously that he would be allowed to finish — and burned afterwards, at playtime.
